correctness.rationale: Exact weighted Paley-Wiener unitary maps the operator to a half-line weighted shift. Its n-th power has explicit density ratio. Differentiation yields the unique sharp positive-parameter optimizer and asymptotic coefficient. Infinite nonatomic near-maximizer subspaces prove approximation distances for all finite ranks and noncompactness. Spectrum follows from power spectral radius in the open quadrant, multiplier essential range on one axis, and infinitely degenerate adjoint eigenvectors on the other axis; the identity is handled separately. All parameters \(\alpha>-1\), \(a,b\ge0\), all n>=1 and finite rank j>=1 are covered. Standalone finite checker passed 1158 tests, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest fully read half-plane Bergman theorem (Elliott-Wynn 2009) covers unweighted composition only, and its norm/spectral-radius equality does not imply the exponential-multiplier phase transition. A fully read weighted-translation spectral theorem (Petkova 2012) assumes positive bounded shift-ratio conditions; the super-Gaussian conjugate weight in the interior quadrant falls outside them. Published records about weighted comp on the disk (Čučković-Zhao 2004), half-plane Hardy (Matache 2019), and abstract weighted-shift realization do not establish the combined alpha-dependent sharp all-power and approximation-number formula. Material access risk is explicitly retained; no bibliographic uniqueness is claimed.

value.rationale: A natural analytic two-parameter family gives an exact spectral phase diagram: combining rightward symbol translation and a decaying analytic multiplier collapses full and essential spectra to zero without making any power compact. Every finite approximation number equals its power norm and the latter has a sharp Gaussian n^2 exponent and alpha-dependent polynomial prefactor. This couples Fredholm spectra, analytic geometry, and approximation theory, and is not an arbitrary substitution or unmotivated finite slice.
